name: Rhoda
overview: Rhoda is a female servant girl mentioned in the New Testament, specifically in Acts 12:13. She served in the household of Mary and is noted for an incident where she did not immediately allow Peter to enter. There is no tribal affiliation or additional personal details recorded about her in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: Rhoda is the only name recorded for this individual, and no specific meaning or divine origin of the name is provided in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Rhoda was a servant in the house of Mary. Beyond this servant relationship, no other family or personal relationships are documented for her.
scriptureSignificance: Rhoda's significance lies in her role during the miraculous deliverance of Peter from prison. Her recognition of Peter's voice and initial hesitation to admit him highlights the human response to divine intervention. This brief but memorable moment underscores the reality of God's power working through ordinary believers in the early church.
